summary: Sumitra Mangesh Katre was a linguist and Indologist who earned a Ph.D. from the University of London. He founded Deccan College, held its Chair of Indo-European Philology (1942–1971), and was later Professor at the University of Texas at Austin (~1971–1976).

Sun-Ah Choi is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD from the University of Chicago under doctoral supervisor Juhyung Rhi, also studying under Richard Neer, Robert S. Nelson, Jaś Elsner, and Aden Kumler.

Sung Bae Park is a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who completed doctoral studies under Lewis Lancaster (~1974–1979). He served as assistant professor at Dongguk University (~1968–1972) and held a post at Stony Brook University from 1977.

Sung Yong Kang is an Indology and philosophy scholar. Educated at Seoul National University and the University of Hamburg (~1999–2006), he held positions at the University of Vienna (~2006–2007) and Seoul National University (~2008).

Sungdoo Ahn is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology who earned his PhD from the University of Hamburg (-2001) under Lambert Schmithausen. He served as Director at Geumgang University and became a Professor at Seoul National University (attested 2013).
Sungtaek Cho is a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar. He has held academic posts at Stony Brook University and at Korea University, where he served as Director (attested 2012–2013).
Sunhee Kim completed a Doctor of Philosophy in Performance Practice at the University of Exeter under the supervision of Phillip B. Zarrilli.

Suniti Kumar Chatterji was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Calcutta, University of London, and Sorbonne under Jules Bloch. He was a longtime professor at the University of Calcutta and National Professor in Humanities (1965–1977).

Surama Dasgupta was an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied under Surendranath Dasgupta, earning degrees from the University of Calcutta and a Ph.D. from the University of Cambridge (-1948). She served as Reader in Philosophy at the University of Lucknow.
Surendra Man Bajracharya is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at Tribhuvan University under doctoral supervisor Bhadra Ratna Bajracharya and co-supervisor Ranjana Bajracharya.

Surendranath Dasgupta was an Indologist and philosopher who earned Ph.Ds from Calcutta and Cambridge. He served as Principal of Sanskrit College (~1931–1942), Principal at Benares Sanskrit College (-1942), and held the Chair of Philosophy at Calcutta University (~1942–1945).
Surendranath Majumdar Sastri was an Indologist and historian who studied under Hara Prasad Sastri and served as a Reader at Patna University (attested 1924).

Surya Kanta was an Indologist and linguist who completed a D.Phil. at the University of Oxford (-1937) under Frederick William Thomas. He served as Reader in Sanskrit at the University of the Punjab (attested 1939).

Surya Kumar Bhuyan was an Indologist and historian educated at Calcutta University and SOAS (PhD 1936). He served as Principal of Cotton University (1918) and Vice Chancellor of Gauhati University (~1957–1960).
Suryanarayana Shukla was a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and philosophy who studied at Rajgopal Sanskrit Mahavidyalaya under Nandakishore Pandey, Ramanujacharya, and Shridatta Pandey.
Susan Andrews is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. She earned her PhD at Columbia University under the doctoral supervision of Chün-fang Yü.
Susan J. Rosenfield is an Indologist who completed her PhD at Harvard University in 2004, studying under scholars including Stephanie W. Jamison and George L. Hart.

Susan L. Beningson is a scholar of sinology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at Columbia University under the doctoral supervision of Robert E. Harrist, Jr. (attested 2009).
Susan L. Huntington is a scholar of history, archaeology, Indology, and Buddhist studies who served as a professor at Ohio State University from ~1971 to 2011.

Susan Naquin is a historian of China and religion who earned her Ph.D. from Yale (~1968–1974). She served as a professor of history at the University of Pennsylvania (1977–1988) and professor at Princeton University (1993–2013).
